examFormat.heading: Claude Certified Architect Professional Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: The practice scenarios set organizational constraints such as data handling, availability, review and budget; compare designs against those constraints.
bestWayToPass: Think across teams: Consider how a design meets different service, governance, and budget needs.
Review security and privacy: Learn how relevant requirements apply to data, model inputs, outputs, and shared responsibilities.
Practise cost estimates: Compare model selection, caching, and batch processing for different workloads.
Plan monitoring: Choose measures for task completion, tool failures, output quality, and escalation.

keyConcepts.h2: Claude Certified Architect Professional: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Enterprise Platform Design
blocks.body: Choose a deployment and data-handling design that meets each team’s regional and availability requirements. Define which policies are common and where controlled differences are allowed.

blocks.heading: Agent Orchestration
blocks.body: Use parallel or delegated agents when their work can be separated and evaluated. Make state, deadlines and completion conditions explicit so the workflow can recover.

blocks.heading: Security and Approval
blocks.body: Treat retrieved content as untrusted input. Enforce permissions, spending limits and consequential approvals in controls outside the model.

blocks.heading: Observability and Response
blocks.body: Trace inputs, tool calls, outputs and termination reasons across steps. Define signals and rollback criteria before deploying changes.

blocks.heading: Cost Governance
blocks.body: Attribute spend to models, teams or workflows. Use model routing and limits only when evaluation shows quality remains acceptable.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Claude Certified Architect Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Separate requirements that must be enforced by the platform from choices that can vary by team or workflow.

blocks.heading: Map non-negotiable controls
blocks.body: Identify data-residency, access, approval and retention requirements before selecting infrastructure.

blocks.heading: Protect consequential actions
blocks.body: Place authorization checks on the execution path and require human review where the impact warrants it.

blocks.heading: Instrument each workflow step
blocks.body: Use traces and evaluation metrics that show where a run stopped or quality changed.

blocks.heading: Measure cost with quality
blocks.body: Attribute cost by workflow and test cheaper model routes against the task’s quality bar.

sampleQuestions.question: A bank must meet regional data-residency requirements and audit decisions across many applications. Which design addresses both?
options: Regional processing nodes with task-based model routing
One shared endpoint that processes all applications in sequence
Separate team deployments with uncoordinated retention
A single model tier with a residency promise in a contract
sampleQuestions.explanation: Regional processing supports data-location constraints; task-based routing can select an appropriate model for each stage.
whyWrong: One shared endpoint that processes all applications in sequence is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Regional processing nodes with task-based model routing.
Separate team deployments with uncoordinated retention is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Regional processing nodes with task-based model routing.
A single model tier with a residency promise in a contract is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Regional processing nodes with task-based model routing.

sampleQuestions.question: Why route simpler tasks to a smaller, faster model?
options: It guarantees identical outputs
Lower cost and latency
It removes the need for evaluations
Smaller models are always more secure
sampleQuestions.explanation: Routing can reduce cost and latency, but each task still needs a quality bar and evaluation.
whyWrong: It guarantees identical outputs is not the best choice because the scenario calls for It can reduce cost and latency if quality remains acceptable.
It removes the need for evaluations is not the best choice because the scenario calls for It can reduce cost and latency if quality remains acceptable.
Smaller models are always more secure is not the best choice because the scenario calls for It can reduce cost and latency if quality remains acceptable.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent can issue refunds up to a limit. Where should the limit be enforced?
options: In a second model’s opinion
In the system prompt only
In deterministic code on the execution path
In a daily report after refunds are issued
sampleQuestions.explanation: A deterministic check before execution prevents a model decision from bypassing the limit.
whyWrong: In a second model’s opinion is not the best choice because the scenario calls for In deterministic code on the execution path.
In the system prompt only is not the best choice because the scenario calls for In deterministic code on the execution path.
In a daily report after refunds are issued is not the best choice because the scenario calls for In deterministic code on the execution path.

sampleQuestions.question: An uploaded document tells an agent to send its context to an outside address. What boundary should the architecture enforce?
options: Refuse every document that contains imperative language
Trust the instruction if the uploader signed in
Let the model decide whether the instruction is safe
Treat document content as data, not as authority
sampleQuestions.explanation: Retrieved document text is untrusted input; system and user policy determine what actions are authorized.
whyWrong: Refuse every document that contains imperative language is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Treat document content as data, not as authority.
Trust the instruction if the uploader signed in is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Treat document content as data, not as authority.
Let the model decide whether the instruction is safe is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Treat document content as data, not as authority.

sampleQuestions.question: A multi-agent workflow sometimes returns incomplete results without an error. What evidence best helps find the failing stage?
options: Step-level traces
Daily token totals
Average end-to-end latency
Count of runs with error status only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Step-level traces show where a run stopped and why, even when the overall run reports success.
whyWrong: Daily token totals is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Per-step traces with inputs and termination reasons.
Average end-to-end latency is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Per-step traces with inputs and termination reasons.
Count of runs with error status only is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Per-step traces with inputs and termination reasons.

sampleQuestions.question: What should trigger rollback of a prompt update?
options: Any increase in response length
Measured evaluation regression
One user comment regardless of evidence
The change being older than one sprint
sampleQuestions.explanation: A defined evaluation can reveal a quality regression and provide a consistent rollback criterion.
whyWrong: Any increase in response length is not the best choice because the scenario calls for A measured regression against the gating evaluation set.
One user comment regardless of evidence is not the best choice because the scenario calls for A measured regression against the gating evaluation set.
The change being older than one sprint is not the best choice because the scenario calls for A measured regression against the gating evaluation set.

sampleQuestions.question: Several teams have different compliance needs on one platform. How should policies be managed?
options: Let the calling app choose policy on each request
Let teams set policy without platform controls
Platform-enforced policy
Apply the strictest rule to every workflow
sampleQuestions.explanation: Central enforcement supports consistent controls while allowing only approved differences across teams.

Let teams set policy without platform controls is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Use central, platform-enforced rules with bounded configuration.

sampleQuestions.question: Costs are increasing faster than usage. What should the platform team do first?
options: Set the same token cap for every team
Move all work to the smallest model
Limit each team to a fixed workflow count
Workflow-level cost attribution
sampleQuestions.explanation: Workflow-level cost attribution helps identify which use cases drive the increase.
whyWrong: Set the same token cap for every team is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Attribute costs by workflow to find the source.
Move all work to the smallest model is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Attribute costs by workflow to find the source.
Limit each team to a fixed workflow count is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Attribute costs by workflow to find the source.

sampleQuestions.question: A long-running agent must resume after its process is lost. What does the design need?
options: Checkpointed state in durable storage
More retries on every tool call
A second identical agent running in parallel
A larger context window
sampleQuestions.explanation: Durable checkpoints let a replacement process resume from completed work rather than start over.
whyWrong: More retries on every tool call is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Checkpointed state in durable storage.
A second identical agent running in parallel is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Checkpointed state in durable storage.
A larger context window is not the best choice because the scenario calls for Checkpointed state in durable storage.

sampleQuestions.question: When is human approval especially useful for an agent action?
options: When the action takes longer than other steps
Irreversible external impact
When it uses several tools
When model confidence is below average, regardless of impact
sampleQuestions.explanation: Irreversible actions with external impact justify a human checkpoint before execution.
whyWrong: When the action takes longer than other steps is not the best choice because the scenario calls for When it is difficult to reverse and affects something outside the system.
When it uses several tools is not the best choice because the scenario calls for When it is difficult to reverse and affects something outside the system.
When model confidence is below average, regardless of impact is not the best choice because the scenario calls for When it is difficult to reverse and affects something outside the system.

sampleQuestions.question: Failures rise after a tool deployment. What should the operations team inspect first?
options: Increase model randomness and wait to see if the failures disappear
Disable alerts so operators are not distracted by transient errors
Review traces and metrics, then compare the failures with deployment changes
Delete failed request records before reviewing the deployment
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use traces and metrics to locate the failing component and compare deployment changes.
whyWrong: Randomness does not identify whether the tool deployment caused the failures.
Disabling alerts hides signals needed to diagnose production impact.
Removing failure records discards evidence needed for diagnosis.

sampleQuestions.question: A regulated workflow moves data through several services. What architecture practice is appropriate?
options: Map data flows, apply least privilege, and audit service boundaries
Share one broad credential across services to simplify operations
Log every sensitive payload in full across all services
Assume each downstream service applies the same access policy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Map data flows, scope access, and audit controls at service boundaries.
whyWrong: Broad shared credentials weaken least privilege and accountability.
Full sensitive payload logs can create unnecessary exposure.
Services need verified controls; policy consistency cannot be assumed.

sampleQuestions.question: Workflow costs rise sharply with volume. What should the team do?
options: Use the highest-capability model for every workflow step
Measure costs by stage and optimize the largest contributors
Disable cost monitoring and wait for monthly billing
Retry failed work without a limit to avoid losing requests
sampleQuestions.explanation: Measure token, tool, and retry costs by stage, then optimize the largest drivers.
whyWrong: That may raise cost further without evidence that each step needs it.
Delayed visibility makes it harder to find the cause of rising spend.
Unbounded retries can increase costs and create additional load.

sampleQuestions.question: A production workflow must keep serving when one model endpoint is unavailable. What should it include?
options: A hidden alternate endpoint that has never been exercised
Unbounded synchronous retries against the unavailable endpoint
A promise to users that service outages cannot happen
A tested fallback or degraded mode with clearly defined limits
sampleQuestions.explanation: A tested fallback or graceful-degradation path with explicit limits.
whyWrong: An untested fallback may fail when the primary endpoint is unavailable.
Repeated synchronous retries can worsen latency and still fail.
A promise does not provide a technical continuity strategy.

sampleQuestions.question: An agent workflow is moving from pilot to production. What should readiness include?
options: Remove evaluation cases to reduce launch preparation time
Rely on informal approval without operational ownership
Define evaluation, monitoring, rollback conditions, and owners
Grant every component unrestricted access to avoid launch delays
sampleQuestions.explanation: Evaluation criteria, monitoring, rollback conditions, and named operational owners.
whyWrong: Removing evaluation weakens evidence about quality and regressions.
Informal approval does not define who monitors or responds to incidents.
Unrestricted access increases risk and does not establish readiness.
